GOAL Produce a sorry-free Lean proof of putnam_2019_b5 in the given file.

FACT The theorem fixes P as the unique degree-1008 interpolant of F at 1009 odd nodes 1, 3, ..., 2017.
FACT The goal requires P.eval 2019 = F 2019 - F 1010 as a real-number identity.
FACT The goal also requires uniqueness: every pair j, k ≥ 1 with F j - F k = P(2019) equals (2019, 1010).
INFER Proving the value needs a closed form for P(2019) from Lagrange interpolation over 1009 nodes, or an equivalent finite-difference argument.
INFER Proving uniqueness needs a separate argument that no other pair of Fibonacci differences hits the same value, handled across all naturals.
FACT Neither step is supported by a tactic that finishes it directly here. `decide` and `norm_num` cannot handle 1009-term rational sums over Fibonacci numbers of about 420 digits, and `native_decide` is forbidden.
FACT Mathlib sources are unavailable, so I cannot look up existing interpolation lemmas beyond what I remember.
INFER A correct formalization is a large development that I cannot complete reliably within this task.

I give up. I did not modify /work/putnam_2019_b5.lean, so it still contains the original `sorry`.
